listing.name: Jet Force Gemini — JetForceGemini-Recomp (VibinToast)
listing.summary: Native Jet Force Gemini with a US ROM picker, portable packages and a separate Linux AppImage.

steps.title: Check the required game files
steps.instruction: Use your own USA z64 ROM, SHA-1 493ced9008dbe932d6e91179b68e8630cf23a023.

steps.title: Start the complete portable package
steps.instruction: Extract the v1.3.2 portable archive into a writable folder. On Windows 10 or 11 with Direct3D 12, open JetForceGeminiRecompiled.exe. For the Linux x64 tarball and AppImage, use glibc 2.35 or newer, Vulkan and system FreeType and D-Bus libraries. For the tarball, open JetForceGeminiRecompiled from the extracted folder. Choose your own ROM in the launcher.

steps.title: Use the prepared Linux copy
steps.instruction: For the prepared portable tarball, select JetForceGeminiRecompiled as the executable and its containing folder as the working directory. Choose Play when you want to start that external copy. The .exe in the next step is for Windows.

warnings: The Windows upstream updater can replace and restart the executable. End the Portcove Play session before using that updater from the standalone player. Keep the data of other Jet Force Gemini implementations separate.

references.title: Choose the Linux package and keep its data
references.instruction: The portable tarball keeps data beside its executable. The AppImage runs from a writable copy in JFG_GAME_DIR, or in JetForceGeminiRecompiled under XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share). Keep saves, settings, mods and texture_packs in the folder you actually use. For Steam Deck, start the AppImage through Steam.

references.title: Replace a Linux 1.2.x copy
references.instruction: Use the current upstream release page for the first update after the repository rename. Keep a backup of your portable folder or AppImage data before replacing it. The 1.3.2 release fixes an upstream Linux crash when selecting a save after restart.

decisions.rationale: The former and current GitHub paths resolve to the recorded numeric repository ID. The maintainer explicitly describes the rename and release history continues across it.

evidence.note: Both provider paths resolve to this recorded repository identity and the current canonical name.
The maintainer describes the repository rename and why the older Linux updater needs a manual download.

decisions.reconsider_when: Reassess if either path resolves to a different provider identity or attributable contradictory continuity evidence appears.

data_locations: the portable executable’s containing folder, including saves, settings, mods and texture packs
